items.name: Corollary 4.2.2 (= Theorem 1.0.7): vanishing of compactly supported completed cohomology above the middle degree
items.statement: Setting of §4: G is a reductive group over ℚ with simply connected derived group and D a G(ℝ)-conjugacy class of u : U(1) → G^ad_ℝ with ad u(−1) a Cartan involution and μ = u_ℂ minuscule; (G, D) is of Hodge type, with a fixed closed embedding (G, D) ↪ (G′, D′) = (Sp_{2g}, D_{Sp_{2g}}); X_K = G(ℚ)∖[D × G(𝔸_f)/K], X*_K its minimal compactification, and X_K** the universal finite map through which X*_K → Y*_{K′} factors for all K′ ⊂ G′(𝔸_f) with K = K′ ∩ G(𝔸_f) (the scheme-theoretic image in Y*_{K′} for K′ small); C is a complete algebraically closed extension of ℚ̄_p (ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p fixed), 𝒳**_K the adic space over C of X_K**, ω_K the pullback of the ample ω_{K′}, and Fl the flag variety of totally isotropic subspaces of C^{2g}; K^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f^p) is contained in the level-N subgroup of G′(𝔸_f^p) for some N ≥ 3 prime to p. The group H̃^i_{c,K^p}(ℤ/p^nℤ), and thus H̃^i_{c,K^p}(ℤ_p), vanishes for i > d = dim_ℂ X_K.
items.note: CC.7 decomposition node boundary-long-exact-sequences-and-the-borel-serre-tower records Corollaries 4.2.2–4.2.3. Proof: by Theorem 4.2.1 it suffices that the spectral space |𝒳**_{K^p}| = lim_{K_p} |𝒳**_{K_pK^p}| has cohomological dimension ≤ d, which follows from the finite levels (de Jong–van der Put, Proposition 2.5.8, or Grothendieck's bound on formal models) and passage to cofiltered limits of spectral spaces.

items.name: Corollary 4.2.3: the Calegari–Emerton conjecture for Borel–Moore completed homology
items.statement: Setting of §4: G is a reductive group over ℚ with simply connected derived group and D a G(ℝ)-conjugacy class of u : U(1) → G^ad_ℝ with ad u(−1) a Cartan involution and μ = u_ℂ minuscule; (G, D) is of Hodge type, with a fixed closed embedding (G, D) ↪ (G′, D′) = (Sp_{2g}, D_{Sp_{2g}}); X_K = G(ℚ)∖[D × G(𝔸_f)/K], X*_K its minimal compactification, and X_K** the universal finite map through which X*_K → Y*_{K′} factors for all K′ ⊂ G′(𝔸_f) with K = K′ ∩ G(𝔸_f) (the scheme-theoretic image in Y*_{K′} for K′ small); C is a complete algebraically closed extension of ℚ̄_p (ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p fixed), 𝒳**_K the adic space over C of X_K**, ω_K the pullback of the ample ω_{K′}, and Fl the flag variety of totally isotropic subspaces of C^{2g}; K^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f^p) is contained in the level-N subgroup of G′(𝔸_f^p) for some N ≥ 3 prime to p. For i > d, H̃_i^BM = 0 and H̃_d^BM is p-torsion free. For i < d, the codimension of H̃_i as a module over the Iwasawa algebra is ≥ d − i.
items.note: CC.7 node boundary-long-exact-sequences-and-the-borel-serre-tower. The proof uses Calegari–Emerton, Theorem 1.1(iii), their Poincaré duality spectral sequence and Venjakob's results on Iwasawa-module codimension; for compact X_K this gives Calegari–Emerton's Conjecture 1.5 with non-strict inequalities.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.1 (with Theorem 1.0.5): Hecke eigenvalues in completed cohomology are interpolated by classical cusp forms
items.statement: Setting of §4: G is a reductive group over ℚ with simply connected derived group and D a G(ℝ)-conjugacy class of u : U(1) → G^ad_ℝ with ad u(−1) a Cartan involution and μ = u_ℂ minuscule; (G, D) is of Hodge type, with a fixed closed embedding (G, D) ↪ (G′, D′) = (Sp_{2g}, D_{Sp_{2g}}); X_K = G(ℚ)∖[D × G(𝔸_f)/K], X*_K its minimal compactification, and X_K** the universal finite map through which X*_K → Y*_{K′} factors for all K′ ⊂ G′(𝔸_f) with K = K′ ∩ G(𝔸_f) (the scheme-theoretic image in Y*_{K′} for K′ small); C is a complete algebraically closed extension of ℚ̄_p (ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p fixed), 𝒳**_K the adic space over C of X_K**, ω_K the pullback of the ample ω_{K′}, and Fl the flag variety of totally isotropic subspaces of C^{2g}; K^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f^p) is contained in the level-N subgroup of G′(𝔸_f^p) for some N ≥ 3 prime to p. Let 𝕋 be the abstract Hecke algebra away from p acting on the H^i_c(X_{K_pK^p}) and on cusp forms. Fix m ≥ 1 and let 𝕋_cl = 𝕋_{cl,m} be 𝕋 with the weakest topology making all maps 𝕋 → End_C(H^0(𝒳*_{K_pK^p}, ω_{K_pK^p}^{⊗mk} ⊗ ℐ)) continuous, for varying k ≥ 1 and K_p ⊂ G(ℚ_p), each target a finite-dimensional C-vector space with the p-adic topology (𝕋_cl need not be separated). Then 𝕋_cl → End_{ℤ/p^nℤ}(H̃^i_{c,K^p}(ℤ/p^nℤ)) is continuous, the target having the weakest topology making End × H̃^i_{c,K^p}(ℤ/p^nℤ) → H̃^i_{c,K^p}(ℤ/p^nℤ) continuous with H̃^i discrete. (Theorem 1.0.5: all Hecke eigenvalues in H̃^i_{c,K^p} are p-adically interpolated by Hecke eigenvalues of classical cusp forms.)
items.note: TC.1 plans 'the approximation/extension lemmas that produce finite-level classical sections after twisting by sufficiently high powers of an ample automorphic line bundle'; the proof uses the formal model 𝔛*_{K_pK^p} with ample ω^int from Lemma 2.1.1 and the vanishing H^1(𝔛*, (ω^int)^{⊗k} ⊗ 𝔍/p^n) = 0 for k divisible enough.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.2: traces of finite generically étale extensions of normal rings are integral
items.statement: Let R be normal and S a finite, generically étale R-algebra, i.e. S[f^{-1}] is finite étale over R[f^{-1}] for some non-zero-divisor f ∈ R. Then tr_{S[f^{-1}]/R[f^{-1}]} : S[f^{-1}] → R[f^{-1}] maps S into R. Moreover, for any integrally closed ideal I ⊂ R with integral closure J ⊂ S, tr(J) ⊂ I.
items.note: R3 constructs traces of finite locally free and finite étale maps; TC.2 needs them for the Hecke trace maps on completed cohomology. Mathlib has the special case in which R and S are integrally closed domains, S finite and torsion-free over R: Algebra.intTrace (Mathlib/RingTheory/IntegralClosure/IntegralRestrict.lean, a linear map B →ₗ[A] A lifting Algebra.trace of the fraction fields), resting on Algebra.isIntegral_trace (Mathlib/RingTheory/Trace/Basic.lean). The lemma as stated is not in the baseline: R normal but not necessarily a domain, S finite and generically étale but neither a domain nor normal, and the ideal statement tr(J) ⊂ I. The status stays planned.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.3: algebraic trace maps on boundary ideals and their compatibility at infinite level
items.statement: Setting of §4: G is a reductive group over ℚ with simply connected derived group and D a G(ℝ)-conjugacy class of u : U(1) → G^ad_ℝ with ad u(−1) a Cartan involution and μ = u_ℂ minuscule; (G, D) is of Hodge type, with a fixed closed embedding (G, D) ↪ (G′, D′) = (Sp_{2g}, D_{Sp_{2g}}); X_K = G(ℚ)∖[D × G(𝔸_f)/K], X*_K its minimal compactification, and X_K** the universal finite map through which X*_K → Y*_{K′} factors for all K′ ⊂ G′(𝔸_f) with K = K′ ∩ G(𝔸_f) (the scheme-theoretic image in Y*_{K′} for K′ small); C is a complete algebraically closed extension of ℚ̄_p (ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p fixed), 𝒳**_K the adic space over C of X_K**, ω_K the pullback of the ample ω_{K′}, and Fl the flag variety of totally isotropic subspaces of C^{2g}; K^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f^p) is contained in the level-N subgroup of G′(𝔸_f^p) for some N ≥ 3 prime to p. Fix J ⊂ {1, …, 2g} containing exactly one of i and g+i for each i = 1, …, g and let 𝒳**_{K^p}(J) = Spa(R_{K^p}, R_{K^p}^+) be the preimage of Fl_J (affinoid perfectoid, the preimage of 𝒳**_{K_pK^p}(J) = Spa(R_{K_pK^p}, R_{K_pK^p}^+) for K_p small, R_{K^p}^+ the p-adic completion of colim R_{K_pK^p}^+); let Spa(R̃_{K_pK^p}, R̃^+_{K_pK^p}) = 𝒳*_{K_pK^p}(J) ⊂ 𝒳*_{K_pK^p} be its preimage, and I^+_{K_pK^p} ⊂ R^+_{K_pK^p}, Ĩ^+_{K_pK^p} ⊂ R̃^+_{K_pK^p}, I^+_{K^p} ⊂ R^+_{K^p} the ideals of functions vanishing along the boundary. Then for all n ≥ 0, I^+_{K^p}/p^n = colim_{K_p} I^+_{K_pK^p}/p^n = colim_{K_p} Ĩ^+_{K_pK^p}/p^n, and for K_1^p ⊂ K_2^p and any K_p the square formed by (tr mod p^n)^a : Ĩ^{+a}_{K_pK_1^p}/p^n → Ĩ^{+a}_{K_pK_2^p}/p^n and tr : I^{+a}_{K_1^p}/p^n → I^{+a}_{K_2^p}/p^n commutes.

items.name: The groups G_0, G, H_0 and the endoscopic embedding η of §5.1
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. K = K_{S^+}K^{S^+} ⊂ G(𝔸_f) = G_0(𝔸_{F^+,f}) is sufficiently small, S^+ a finite set of finite places of F^+ containing those above p and those where F ramifies, K^{S^+} a product of hyperspecial K_v; S is the set of places of F above S^+.
items.note: The unitary endoscopic data are ET's (ET.0/ET.4); the symplectic twisted endoscopic datum for GL_{2n+1} is part of ML.4's classical-group classification input.

items.name: Proposition 5.1.1: holomorphic discrete series of Sp_{2n}(ℝ) and U(n,n) with scalar minimal K-type
items.statement: Let 𝒢 = Sp_{2n}/ℝ, resp. U(n,n)/ℝ, with maximal compact K ⊂ 𝒢(ℝ), standard Borel ℬ with torus 𝒯, X*(𝒯_ℂ) = ℤ^n resp. ℤ^{2n}. Let χ : K ≅ U(n) → ℂ^×, g_0 ↦ det(g_0), resp. χ : K ≅ U(n) × U(n) → ℂ^×, (g_1, g_2) ↦ det(g_1)det(g_2)^{-1}. For k > n, resp. k ≥ n, there is a unique discrete series representation π_k of 𝒢 with minimal K-type χ^{⊗k}, and it has infinitesimal character (k−1, k−2, …, k−n) ∈ ℝ^n, resp. (k−½, k−3/2, …, k−n+½, n−½−k, …, 3/2−k, ½−k) ∈ ℝ^{2n}.
items.note: Missing: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1 builds (𝔤, K)-module foundations and AF.4 infinitesimal characters of cohomological representations, and ET.1 the unitary discrete-series pseudocoefficients, but no layer identifies the holomorphic discrete series of Sp_{2n}(ℝ) and U(n,n) by their scalar minimal K-type. Routed as a source of AF.4 (with AF.1), where the accepted routes of PAPER-PILLONI-20 (route 13), PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 (route 10) and PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26 (route 14) already put (limits of) discrete series, their Harish-Chandra parameters and holomorphic limits of discrete series.

items.name: Holomorphic cusp forms of weight k as automorphic representations with π_∞ ≅ π_k
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. 𝕋 acts on H^0(X*_K, ω_K^{⊗k} ⊗ ℐ) ⊗_ℂ C = H^0(𝒳*_K, ω_K^{⊗k} ⊗ ℐ) (ω from the Siegel ample bundle, ℐ the boundary ideal); the image of 𝕋 ⊗ ℂ in End_ℂ(H^0(X*_K, ω_K^{⊗k} ⊗ ℐ)) is a product of copies of ℂ, because the Petersson inner product is positive definite and the adjoint of a Hecke operator is a Hecke operator; each character x of this image comes from a cuspidal automorphic representation π of G_0/F^+, unramified outside S^+ with Satake parameters given by x, with π_v ≅ π_k for v | ∞.
items.locator: §5.1, the paragraph before Corollary 5.1.7, p. 1035, and the proof of Corollary 5.1.7, p. 1036
items.note: Missing: AutomorphicBundles B4 plans classical forms as sections of the canonical and subcanonical extensions, explicitly including Siegel data and a unitary PEL example, and AF.5 plans the automorphic dictionary only for GL_1 and GL_2/ℚ; the passage between H^0(X*_K, ω_K^k ⊗ ℐ) and cuspidal π with π_∞ ≅ π_k (with Hecke semisimplicity from the Petersson product) is planned nowhere. The accepted extractions PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 and -20 (thm-5-2-1, automorphic-representation-of-eigenform), PAPER-PILLONI-20 (holomorphic-cusp-forms-embed-in-H0) and PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26 (cuspidal-limits-contribute-to-coherent-cohomology) route exactly this passage to the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes ('Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes', parent AutomorphicBundles, area langlands); this item joins it.

items.name: Theorem 5.1.2 (Arthur, Mok) as corrected: weak endoscopic transfer of π with π_∞ ≅ π_k to GL_h
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of G_0 and fix k > n, resp. k ≥ n, with π_v ≅ π_k (Proposition 5.1.1) for v | ∞. There are cuspidal automorphic representations Π_1, …, Π_m of GL_{n_1}/F, …, GL_{n_m}/F and integers ℓ_1, …, ℓ_m ≥ 1 with n_1ℓ_1 + ⋯ + n_mℓ_m = h and (Π_i^∨)^c ≅ Π_i (c complex conjugation if F is CM, the identity if F is totally real), such that for every finite place v of F over a place v^+ of F^+ at which π_{v^+} is unramified, all Π_{iv} are unramified and η_{v^+*}φ_{π_{v^+}} = ⊕_{i=1}^m (φ_{Π_{iv}}|·|^{(1−ℓ_i)/2} ⊕ φ_{Π_{iv}}|·|^{(3−ℓ_i)/2} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ φ_{Π_{iv}}|·|^{(ℓ_i−1)/2}) as h-dimensional representations of W_{F_v}, where φ_{π_{v^+}} : W_{F^+_{v^+}} → ᴸG_{0,v^+} and φ_{Π_{iv}} : W_{F_v} → ᴸGL_{n_i,v} are the unramified L-parameters (printed: exponent (ℓ_i − i)/2 and target ᴸGL_{h,v}; sourceIssues E8). Moreover, for v | ∞, Π_{iv}|·|^{(h−ℓ_i)/2} is regular L-algebraic (Buzzard–Gee), and by Remark 5.1.3 the infinitesimal characters of the Π_{iv}|·|^{(2j−ℓ_i−1)/2}, j = 1, …, ℓ_i, combine to (k−1, …, k−n, 0, n−k, …, 1−k) if F is totally real, resp. (k−½, …, k−n+½, n−½−k, …, ½−k) if F is CM.
items.note: Conditional in the paper on the stabilization of the twisted trace formula. ML.4 registers Arthur's (symplectic) and Mok's (unitary) classifications with their conditional hypotheses; the unitary base-change identities at split and unramified places are ET.7a's pure automorphic branch (Shin's results, cf. Remark 5.4.6).

items.name: Theorem 5.1.4: Galois representations for regular algebraic conjugate self-dual cuspidal representations
items.statement: Let F be totally real or CM and Π a cuspidal automorphic representation of Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n with (Π^∨)^c ≅ Π and Π|·|^{k/2} regular L-algebraic for some integer k. Then there is a continuous semisimple σ_Π : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) with (σ_Π^∨)^c ≅ σ_Πχ_p^k (χ_p the p-adic cyclotomic character; local class field theory normalized so that geometric Frobenius elements match uniformizers) such that for every finite place v with Π_v unramified, σ_Π is unramified at v and φ_{Π_v} = σ_Π|_{W_{F_v}}|·|^{k/2} up to (Frobenius-)semisimplification. (Remark 5.1.5: Π′ = Π|·|^{(k+1−n)/2} is regular C-algebraic with (Π′^∨)^c ≅ Π′ ⊗ χ, χ = |·|^{n−1−k} (printed |·|^{n+1−k}; see sourceIssues).)
items.note: Due to Clozel, Kottwitz, Harris–Taylor, Shin, Chenevier–Harris and others; AG2.2–AG2.3 construct the polarized regular algebraic systems.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.6(i): the unramified Hecke algebra of Sp_{2n} and the transfer to GL_{2n+1}
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. Let F be totally real and v ∉ S^+, q_v the residue cardinality and q_v^{1/2} ∈ ℤ̄_p the image of the positive square root. The Satake transform gives 𝕋_v[q_v^{1/2}] ≅ ℤ_p[q_v^{1/2}][X_1^{±1}, …, X_n^{±1}]^{S_n⋉(ℤ/2)^n}, where 𝕋_v = ℤ_p[G_0(F_v^+)//K_v]; the unramified transfer from G_0(F_v^+) to GL_{2n+1}(F_v^+) is dual to the map from ℤ_p[q_v^{1/2}][Y_1^{±1}, …, Y_{2n+1}^{±1}]^{S_{2n+1}} sending {Y_1, …, Y_{2n+1}} to {X_1^{±1}, …, X_n^{±1}, 1}. If T_{i,v} is the image of the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Y_j, i = 1, …, 2n+1, then T_{i,v} ∈ 𝕋_v.
items.note: IHG.3 plans the integral spherical normalization and its conversions; TC.3 the Hecke polynomial identities through Satake.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.6(ii)–(iii): the unramified Hecke algebra of the quasisplit unitary group at split and inert places
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. Let F be CM and v ∉ S^+. (ii) If v splits in F, with a fixed lift ṽ, then G_0(F_v^+) ≅ GL_{2n}(F_ṽ), 𝕋_v[q_v^{1/2}] ≅ ℤ_p[q_v^{1/2}][X_1^{±1}, …, X_{2n}^{±1}]^{S_{2n}}, the unramified transfer is the identity, and for T_{i,ṽ} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in X_1, …, X_{2n}, q_v^{i/2}T_{i,ṽ} ∈ 𝕋_v (the other choice of ṽ replaces X_i by X_i^{-1}). (iii) If v is inert in F, 𝕋_v[q_v^{1/2}] ≅ ℤ_p[q_v^{1/2}][X_1^{±1}, …, X_n^{±1}]^{S_n⋉(ℤ/2)^n}, the transfer to GL_{2n}(F_v) is dual to {Y_1, …, Y_{2n}} ↦ {X_1^{±1}, …, X_n^{±1}}, and the images T_{i,v} of the elementary symmetric polynomials in the Y_j lie in 𝕋_v.

items.name: Corollary 5.1.7: Galois representations for Hecke eigensystems in holomorphic cusp forms of weight k
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. Fix k > n, resp. k ≥ n (F totally real, resp. CM); δ = 0 if F is totally real and δ = 1 if F is CM. Let 𝕋_{K,k} be the image of 𝕋 in End_C(H^0(X*_K, ω_K^{⊗k} ⊗ ℐ) ⊗_ℂ C). Then 𝕋_{K,k} is flat over ℤ_p and 𝕋_{K,k}[p^{-1}] is finite étale over ℚ_p. For any x ∈ (Spec 𝕋_{K,k})(ℚ̄_p) there is a continuous semisimple σ_x : G_{F,S} → GL_h(ℚ̄_p) with (σ_x^∨)^c ≅ σ_xχ_p^δ such that for every finite place v ∉ S, det(1 − X Frob_v | σ_x) = 1 − (q_v^{δ/2}T_{1,v})(x)X + (q_v^{2δ/2}T_{2,v})(x)X² − ⋯ + (−1)^h(q_v^{hδ/2}T_{h,v})(x)X^h, Frob_v the geometric Frobenius and q_v the residue cardinality of F at v.
items.note: Proof: σ_x = ⊕_i(σ_i ⊕ σ_iχ_p^{-1} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ σ_iχ_p^{1−ℓ_i}) from Theorem 5.1.2 and Theorem 5.1.4 applied to Π_i|·|^{(δ+1−ℓ_i)/2}. The symplectic branch inherits Arthur's hypothesis (ML.4).

items.name: Definition 5.1.8 and Remark 5.1.9: determinants, their (nonstandard) characteristic polynomials and continuity
items.statement: Let A be a (topological) ring and G a (topological) group. A d-dimensional determinant is an A-polynomial law D : A[G] → A which is multiplicative and homogeneous of degree d; for g ∈ G, D(1 − Xg) ∈ A[X] is the characteristic polynomial of g, and D is continuous if g ↦ D(1 − Xg), G → A[X], is continuous (Chenevier, 2.30). More generally, for an A-algebra B a multiplicative A-polynomial law A[G] → B homogeneous of degree d is a determinant of dimension d with values in B; equivalently a multiplicative B-polynomial law B[G] → B homogeneous of degree d.
items.note: IHG.0 packet nodes determinant, characteristic-polynomial, continuous-determinant and determinant-base-change (from Chenevier's paper).

items.name: Corollary 5.1.10: the Hecke-valued determinant on classical cusp forms
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. There is a unique continuous h-dimensional determinant D of G_{F,S} with values in 𝕋_{K,k} such that D(1 − X Frob_v) = 1 − q_v^{δ/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2δ/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^h q_v^{hδ/2}T_{h,v}X^h for all finite places v ∉ S.
items.note: 𝕋_{K,k} is flat with 𝕋_{K,k}[1/p] finite étale; the determinant is glued from the σ_x (Chenevier).

items.name: Corollary 5.1.11: determinants over discrete continuous quotients of the classical Hecke algebra
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. Let 𝕋_cl = 𝕋_{cl,m} be as in Theorem 4.3.1, with m > n if F is totally real and m ≥ n if F is CM (the hypothesis is not printed; see sourceIssues). For any continuous quotient 𝕋_cl → A with A discrete there is a unique continuous h-dimensional determinant D of G_{F,S} with values in A such that D(1 − X Frob_v) = 1 − q_v^{δ/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2δ/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^h q_v^{hδ/2}T_{h,v}X^h for all finite places v ∉ S.
items.note: The proof glues determinants modulo I_1 and I_2 to one modulo I_1 ∩ I_2 (Chenevier, Example 2.32); as in PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/94.

items.name: Definition 5.2.1 and Lemma 5.2.2 as corrected: the locally symmetric spaces of the parabolic and its Levi
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. Fix a parabolic P ⊂ G with Levi M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n and unipotent radical U. For compact open K_M ⊂ M(𝔸_f), X^M_{K_M} = M(ℚ)∖[(M(ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × M(𝔸_f)/K_M]; for compact open K_P ⊂ P(𝔸_f), X^P_{K_P} = P(ℚ)∖[(P(ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × P(𝔸_f)/K_P] (K_∞ maximal compact, ℝ_{>0} the positive scalars). Lemma 5.2.2: the image K_P^M ⊂ M(𝔸_f) of K_P is compact open, and there is a natural projection X^P_{K_P} → X^M_{K_P^M} (printed X^P_{X_P} → X^M_{X_P^M}; sourceIssues E9) which is a bundle with fibres (S^1)^k, k = dim U.
items.note: ALS.2: boundary strata are fibrations with nilmanifold fibres over Levi arithmetic quotients.

items.name: The Borel–Serre boundary, its long exact sequence and the parabolic stratum
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. For K sufficiently small, the Borel–Serre compactification X_K^BS is a compact real manifold with corners and X_K ↪ X_K^BS is a homotopy equivalence, giving ⋯ → H^i_c(X_K, ℤ/p^m) → H^i(X_K, ℤ/p^m) → H^i(X_K^BS ∖ X_K, ℤ/p^m) → ⋯. For K^P = K ∩ P(𝔸_f) there is an open embedding X^P_{K^P} ↪ X_K^BS ∖ X_K, hence maps H^i_c(X^P_{K^P}, ℤ/p^m) → H^i(X_K^BS ∖ X_K, ℤ/p^m) → H^i(X^P_{K^P}, ℤ/p^m); with K^M = K^P ∩ M(𝔸_f) (assumed equal to the image of K^P), pullback along the section X^M_{K^M} ↪ X^P_{K^P} (printed '→ K^P_{K^P}'; sourceIssues E10) gives H^i(X^P_{K^P}) → H^i(X^M_{K^M}), and the resulting diagram with H^i_c(X^M_{K^M}) → H^i_c(X^P_{K^P}) commutes. The interior cohomology is H^i_!(X^M_{K^M}, ℤ/p^m) = im(H^i_c(X^M_{K^M}, ℤ/p^m) → H^i(X^M_{K^M}, ℤ/p^m)).
items.note: ALS.2 (Borel–Serre and homotopy equivalence) and ALS.4 (the triangle RΓ_c → RΓ → RΓ_∂ and the Levi strata).

items.name: The Hecke algebras 𝕋_{K^{S^+}}, 𝕋_{K^{P,S^+}}, 𝕋_{K^{M,S^+}}, the unnormalized Satake transform and their actions on boundary cohomology
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. 𝕋_{K^{S^+}} = ℤ_p[G_0(𝔸^{S^+}_{F^+,f})//K^{S^+}], 𝕋_{K^{P,S^+}} = ℤ_p[P_0(𝔸^{S^+}_{F^+,f})//K^{P,S^+}], 𝕋_{K^{M,S^+}} = ℤ_p[M_0(𝔸^{S^+}_{F^+,f})//K^{M,S^+}] (P = Res P_0, M_0 = Res_{F/F^+}GL_n). Restriction of functions 𝕋_{K^{S^+}} → 𝕋_{K^{P,S^+}} followed by integration along unipotent fibres 𝕋_{K^{P,S^+}} → 𝕋_{K^{M,S^+}} is the unnormalized Satake transform. 𝕋_{K^{S^+}} acts on H^i(X_K^BS ∖ X_K, ℤ/p^m); 𝕋_{K^{P,S^+}} → Hom(H^i_c(X^P_{K^P}), H^i(X^P_{K^P})) and 𝕋_{K^{M,S^+}} → Hom(H^i_c(X^M_{K^M}), H^i(X^M_{K^M})) (independent of whether one acts on H_c or H), and 𝕋_{K^{M,S^+}} → End(H^i_!(X^M_{K^M}, ℤ/p^m)) has the same kernel as the latter map.
items.note: ALS.4 compares the boundary Hecke action with parabolic induction and Satake transforms; TC.3 calculates it through the Levi Satake map.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.3 and Corollary 5.2.4: compatibility of the boundary Hecke action with the Levi
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. Lemma 5.2.3: the diagram with rows 𝕋_{K^{S^+}} → End(H^i(X_K^BS ∖ X_K, ℤ/p^m)), 𝕋_{K^{P,S^+}} → Hom(H^i_c(X^P_{K^P}), H^i(X^P_{K^P})), 𝕋_{K^{M,S^+}} → Hom(H^i_c(X^M_{K^M}), H^i(X^M_{K^M})) and the restriction/integration and cohomological maps as columns commutes. Corollary 5.2.4: with 𝕋̄_{K^{S^+}} the image of 𝕋_{K^{S^+}} in End(H^i(X_K^BS ∖ X_K, ℤ/p^m)) and 𝕋̄_{K^{M,S^+}} the image of 𝕋_{K^{M,S^+}} in End(H^i_!(X^M_{K^M}, ℤ/p^m)), the unnormalized Satake transform induces a commutative square of ℤ_p-algebras 𝕋_{K^{S^+}} → 𝕋̄_{K^{S^+}} → 𝕋̄_{K^{M,S^+}}.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.5(i): the Satake transform to the Siegel Levi for Sp_{2n} and the factorization of the Hecke polynomial
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. Let F be totally real (v = v^+ ∉ S). The unnormalized Satake transform 𝕋_v[q_v^{1/2}] ≅ ℤ_p[q_v^{1/2}][X_1^{±1}, …, X_n^{±1}]^{S_n⋉(ℤ/2)^n} → 𝕋_{K_v^M}[q_v^{1/2}] ≅ ℤ_p[q_v^{1/2}][X_1^{±1}, …, X_n^{±1}]^{S_n} sends {X_1^{±1}, …, X_n^{±1}} to {(q_v^{(n+1)/2}X_1)^{±1}, …, (q_v^{(n+1)/2}X_n)^{±1}}. With T^M_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in X_1, …, X_n, q_v^{i(n+1)/2}T^M_{i,v} ∈ 𝕋_{K_v^M}, and 1 − T_{1,v}X + T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ − T_{2n+1,v}X^{2n+1} maps to (1 − X)·(1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T^M_{1,v}X + ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T^M_{n,v}X^n)·(1 − q_v^{−(n+1)/2}(T^M_{n−1,v}/T^M_{n,v})X + ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{−n(n+1)/2}(1/T^M_{n,v})X^n).
items.note: TC.3: 'Prove polynomial identities relating Levi factors, contragredients and character twists to the ambient Hecke polynomial'.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.5(ii)–(iii): the Satake transform to the Siegel Levi for the unitary group
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. Let F be CM, v ∉ S over v^+ ∉ S^+. (ii) If v^+ splits (v̄ the conjugate place, q_{v^+} = q_v), the unnormalized Satake transform ℤ_p[q_v^{1/2}][X_1^{±1}, …, X_{2n}^{±1}]^{S_{2n}} → ℤ_p[q_v^{1/2}][X_1^{±1}, …, X_n^{±1}, Y_1^{±1}, …, Y_n^{±1}]^{S_n×S_n} sends {X_1, …, X_{2n}} to {q_v^{n/2}X_1, …, q_v^{n/2}X_n, q_v^{−n/2}Y_1, …, q_v^{−n/2}Y_n}; with T^M_{i,v} (resp. T^M_{i,v̄}) the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in X_1, …, X_n (resp. Y_1^{-1}, …, Y_n^{-1}), q_v^{i(n+1)/2}T^M_{i,v} ∈ 𝕋_{K^M_{v^+}}, and 1 − q_v^{1/2}T_{1,v}X + q_vT_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + q_v^nT_{2n,v}X^{2n} ↦ (1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T^M_{1,v}X + ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T^M_{n,v}X^n)·(1 − q_v^{−(n−1)/2}(T^M_{n−1,v̄}/T^M_{n,v̄})X + ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{−n(n−1)/2}(1/T^M_{n,v̄})X^n). (iii) If v is inert (q_v = q_{v^+}², q_v^{1/2} = q_{v^+}), the transform sends {X_i^{±1}} to {(q_v^{n/2}X_i)^{±1}}, T^M_{i,v} ∈ 𝕋_{K^M_{v^+}}, and the same factorization holds with v̄ replaced by v.

items.name: The polynomials P_v(X), P_v^∨(X) and P̃_v(X)
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. 𝕋_{K^{M,S^+}} = ⊗_{v∉S}𝕋_v^M with 𝕋_v^M[q_v^{1/2}] ≅ ℤ_p[q_v^{1/2}][X_1^{±1}, …, X_n^{±1}]^{S_n}; T^M_{i,v} is the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial and q_v^{i(n+1)/2}T^M_{i,v} ∈ 𝕋_v^M. P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T^M_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T^M_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T^M_{n,v}X^n and P_v^∨(X) = 1 − q_v^{−(n+1)/2}(T^M_{n−1,v}/T^M_{n,v})X + ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{−n(n+1)/2}(1/T^M_{n,v})X^n in 𝕋_v^M[X] (the polynomial with constant term 1 whose zeroes are the inverses of those of P_v). P̃_v(X) = (1 − X)P_v(X)P_v^∨(X) if F is totally real, and P̃_v(X) = P_v(X)P^∨_{v^c}(q_vX) ∈ 𝕋_{K^M_{v^+}}[X] if F is CM (v^c the conjugate place).

items.name: Corollary 5.2.6: a determinant for the interior cohomology of the Levi, modulo an ideal I with I^{2(d+1)} = 0
items.statement: Setting of §5.1: F is totally real or CM, F^+ its maximal totally real subfield; G_0 = Sp_{2n}/F^+ if F is totally real and G_0 = U/F^+ the quasisplit unitary group (a form of GL_{2n}) for F/F^+ if F is CM; G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0, with the standard D, is of Hodge type and has M = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n as a maximal Levi; G is a twisted endoscopic group of H = Res_{F/ℚ}H_0, H_0 = GL_h/F, h = 2n+1 (totally real) or 2n (CM), via the standard embedding η : ᴸG_0 ↪ ᴸRes_{F/F^+}H_0. Let d be the complex dimension of X_K. There is an ideal I ⊂ 𝕋̄_{K^{M,S^+}} = im(𝕋_{K^{M,S^+}} → End_{ℤ/p^m}(H^i_!(X^M_{K^M}, ℤ/p^m))) with I^{2(d+1)} = 0 and a continuous h-dimensional determinant D of G_{F,S} with values in A = 𝕋̄_{K^{M,S^+}}/I satisfying D(1 − X Frob_v) = P̃_v(X) for all finite v ∉ S.
items.note: Proof: Poincaré duality reduces to H^i_c; Hochschild–Serre from completed cohomology, Corollary 4.2.2's amplitude, Theorem 4.3.1 and Corollary 5.1.11 give determinants modulo J_1, J_2 with J_i^{d+1} = 0, and a two-step filtration of the boundary gives the exponent 2(d+1).

items.name: Corollary 5.2.7: the 2n+1 or 2n-dimensional determinant for the interior cohomology of GL_n over F
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. Let K ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) be sufficiently small (possible by shrinking at one v ∈ S not dividing p), of the form K_SK^S with K_S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,S}) compact open and torsion-free, and 𝕋_{F,S}(K, i, m) = im(𝕋_{F,S} → End_{ℤ/p^m}(H^i_!(X_K, ℤ/p^m))). Then there is an ideal I ⊂ 𝕋_{F,S}(K, i, m) with I^{2(d+1)} = 0 and a continuous h-dimensional determinant D̃ of G_{F,S} with values in 𝕋_{F,S}(K, i, m)/I satisfying D̃(1 − X Frob_v) = P̃_v(X) for all v ∉ S.
items.note: The locally symmetric spaces and Hecke algebras for GL_n/F are ALS.0 and ALS.3 objects.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.1: the n-dimensional determinant for the interior cohomology of GL_n, modulo J with J^{4(d+1)} = 0
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. There is an ideal J ⊂ 𝕋_{F,S}(K, i, m) with J^{4(d+1)} = 0 and a continuous n-dimensional determinant D of G_{F,S} with values in 𝕋_{F,S}(K, i, m)/J satisfying D(1 − X Frob_v) = P_v(X) for all v ∉ S.
items.note: TC.3: 'Build the abstract factor-separation lemma using actual auxiliary characters with the source's separation property … Include the case of nilpotent coefficient quotients'.

items.name: The twisted polynomials of §5.3: characters χ of odd order, P_{v,χ}, P̃_{v,χ} and the determinants D̃_χ
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. A_0 = 𝕋_{F,S}(K, i, m) (a finite ring) and A = A_0 ⊗_{ℤ_p} W(𝔽̄_p). For a continuous character χ : G_{F,S} → W(𝔽̄_p)^× of odd order prime to p, P_{v,χ}(X) = P_v(X/χ(Frob_v)), P^∨_{v,χ}(X) = P_v^∨(χ(Frob_v)X), and P̃_{v,χ}(X) = (1 − X)P_{v,χ}(X)P^∨_{v,χ}(X) (F totally real) or P_{v,χ}(X)P^∨_{v^c,χ}(q_vX) (F CM). There is a determinant D̃_χ with values in A/I_χ, I_χ^{2(d+1)} = 0, with D̃_χ(1 − X Frob_v) = P̃_{v,χ}(X) for all v ∉ S (Corollary 5.2.7 applied to twisted coefficients).

items.name: Lemmas 5.3.2–5.3.3: an auxiliary extension L_0 and factorization of the twisted determinants
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. (5.3.2) There is a finite extension L_0/F, Galois over F^+, such that for all v ∉ S split in L_0, P̄_v(X) = P̄_{v^c}(X) = (1 − X)^n (the reductions), and q_v ≡ 1 mod p if F is CM. (5.3.3) With ℓ ≠ p a sufficiently large auxiliary prime not dividing [L_0:F], S_ℓ = S ∪ {places above ℓ}, F^{cycl_ℓ} the cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension and L^{∞_ℓ} the maximal pro-p extension of L_0·F^{cycl_ℓ} unramified outside S_ℓ, for any character χ : Gal(F^{cycl_ℓ}/F) ≅ ℤ_ℓ → W(𝔽̄_p)^× the determinant D̃_χ of G_{F,S_ℓ} factors over Gal(L^{∞_ℓ}/F).

items.name: Lemma 5.3.4 and Corollary 5.3.5: continuous interpolation g ↦ P_g of the Hecke polynomials
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. (5.3.4) There is a unique continuous function g ↦ P_g : Gal(L^{∞_ℓ}/F) ∖ Gal(L^{∞_ℓ}/F^{cycl_ℓ}) → (A_0/I_0)[X] with P_{Frob_v} = P_v for all v ∉ S_ℓ. (5.3.5) There is a unique continuous function g ↦ P_g : G_{F,S} → (A_0/I_0)[X] with P_{Frob_v} = P_v for all v ∉ S (I_0 the nilpotent ideal of the proof).

items.name: Lemmas 5.3.6–5.3.7: the universal twisted determinant over A[T^{±1}]
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. Let F̃/F be a finite Galois extension unramified outside S through which the function g ↦ P_g of Corollary 5.3.5 factors. Enlarge it by a primitive p-power root of unity so that some g ↦ q_g ∈ A_0/I_0 interpolates Frob_v ↦ q_v, and in the CM case take F̃ Galois over F^+, so that g ↦ g^c is defined on conjugacy classes. Let G = Gal(F̃/F) and fix a new prime ℓ ≠ p, ℓ ≥ 3, not dividing [F̃:F]. Then: (5.3.6) there is an ideal I ⊂ A[T^{±1}] containing I_0·A[T^{±1}] with I^{4(d+1)} = 0 and an h-dimensional determinant D̃_I : A[G][V^{±1}] → A[T^{±1}]/I with D̃_I(1 − XV^kg) = (1 − X)P_g(X/T^k)P_g^∨(T^kX) if F is totally real, resp. P_g(X/T^k)P^∨_{g^c}(T^kq_gX) if F is CM, for all g ∈ G, k ∈ ℤ. (5.3.7) There is an ideal J ⊂ A with I_0·A ⊂ J, J^{4(d+1)} = 0, and an h-dimensional determinant D̃ : A[G][V^{±1}] → (A/J)[T^{±1}] with the same formulas.

items.name: Lemma 5.3.8 (with Remark 5.3.9): extracting determinants from a twisted product determinant
items.statement: Let G be a group and R a ring. For m ∈ ℤ let g ↦ P_g^{(m)}(X) : G → R[X] take values in polynomials of degree n_m with constant term 1, n_m = 0 for almost all m, and n = Σ_m n_m. Assume there is an n-dimensional determinant D̃ : R[G][V^{±1}] → R[T^{±1}] with D̃(1 − V^kXg) = ∏_{m∈ℤ} P_g^{(m)}(T^{km}X) in R[T^{±1}][X] for all g ∈ G, k ∈ ℤ. Then for every m there is an n_m-dimensional determinant D^{(m)} : R[G] → R with D^{(m)}(1 − Xg) = P_g^{(m)}(X) for all g ∈ G. (Remark 5.3.9: if ⊕_m π_m ⊗ χ^m exists as a representation of G × ℤ for every character χ of ℤ, then every π_m exists.)
items.note: The abstract factor-separation lemma TC.3 plans; R[G][V^{±1}] = R[G × ℤ].

items.name: Lemma 5.3.10: uniqueness of the decomposition of a power series by T-weight
items.statement: Let S be a commutative ring and Q ∈ S[T^{±1}][[X]] with Q ≡ 1 mod X. There is at most one way to write Q = ∏_{m∈ℤ} Q_m with Q_m ∈ S[[XT^m]], Q_m ≡ 1 mod X, almost all equal to 1. If Q ∈ S[T^{±1}][X], then all Q_m ∈ S[XT^m].

items.name: Lemmas 5.3.11–5.3.12: the multiplicative maps D_0^{(m)}
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 5.3.8: (5.3.11) for any R-algebra S there are unique multiplicative maps D_0^{(m)} : 1 + US[G][[U]] → 1 + US[[U]] with D̃(f(XV)) = ∏_{m∈ℤ} D_0^{(m)}(f(XT^m)) in S[T^{±1}][[X]] for all f(U) ∈ 1 + US[G][[U]]; they satisfy D_0^{(m)}(1 − U^axg) = P_g^{(m)}(U^ax) for a ≥ 1, x ∈ S, g ∈ G, and map 1 + US[G][U] into 1 + US[U]. (5.3.12) For a nilpotent ideal I ⊂ S and f ∈ 1 + US[G][U] with f ≡ 1 mod I and f|_{U=1} = 1, D_0^{(m)}(f)|_{U=1} = 1.

items.name: Lemma 5.3.13: multiplicative polynomial laws decompose into homogeneous ones
items.statement: Let R[G] → R be a multiplicative R-polynomial law. Then for some integer N there is a decomposition R = R_0 × ⋯ × R_N × R_∞ into direct factors such that for 0 ≤ d ≤ N the induced multiplicative R_d-polynomial law R_d[G] → R_d is homogeneous of degree d (a determinant of dimension d), and R_∞[G] → R_∞ is constantly 0.
items.note: IHG.0 plans homogeneous and multiplicative polynomial laws (Roby, Chenevier); the decomposition by degree is part of that theory as used in TC.3's factor extraction.

items.name: The coefficient systems ℳ_{ξ,K} and the Hecke algebras 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i, m)
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. In §5.4, K ⊂ ∏_v GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}), i.e. K = K_SK^S with K_S any compact open subgroup of ∏_{v∈S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); if K is not sufficiently small, X_K is regarded as a stacky quotient. Fix an algebraic representation ξ of Res_{𝒪_F/ℤ}GL_n with coefficients in a finite free ℤ̄_p-module M_ξ; it defines a local system ℳ_{ξ,K} of ℤ̄_p-modules on X_K for every such K. By the Satake isomorphism 𝕋_v[q_v^{1/2}] ≅ ℤ_p[q_v^{1/2}][X_1^{±1}, …, X_n^{±1}]^{S_n}, and q_v^{i(n+1)/2}T_{i,v} ∈ 𝕋_v. 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i, m) = im(𝕋_{F,S} → End_{ℤ̄_p/p^m}(H^i(X_K, ℳ_{ξ,K}/p^m))).
items.note: ALS.1: local systems from algebraic representations with stable lattices.

items.name: Theorem 5.4.1: Galois determinants for torsion in the cohomology of GL_n over totally real and CM fields
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. There is an integer N = N([F:ℚ], n), depending only on [F:ℚ] and n, such that for any compact open K = K_SK^S ⊂ ∏_v GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}) ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) as in §5.4 (K_S any compact open subgroup of ∏_{v∈S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}), K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})), any algebraic representation ξ and any integers i, m ≥ 0: there is an ideal I ⊂ 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i, m) with I^N = 0 and an n-dimensional continuous determinant D of G_{F,S} with values in 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i, m)/I satisfying D(1 − X Frob_v) = P_v(X) for all v ∉ S.
items.note: The main theorem. Following the accepted extractions PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/72, PAPER-CARAIANI-NEWTON-23/thm-2-1-24 and PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-24/2, which cite it, it is planned by TC.2–TC.4 with IHG.5's nilpotent descent. TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure's summary says formalizing this final theorem is 'not an additional requirement'; that is a scope statement about the roadmap's target, while TC.4's contract (§5.4: 'compatibility checks and reusable specialization infrastructure') and IHG.5 plan exactly its assembly. Proof: Hochschild–Serre along a normal K′ ⊂ K on which ℳ_{ξ,K′}/p^m is trivial reduces to K small and ξ trivial; the Borel–Serre sequence splits the Hecke action into the interior part (Theorem 5.3.1) and the boundary part, which is expressed through the locally symmetric spaces of GL_{n′}, n′ < n, and handled by induction (left in the paper as 'an easy exercise', citing Caraiani–Le Hung §3, so the TC.3 design has to write it out); the two are glued along a square-zero kernel by Chenevier, Corollary 1.14. The totally real case assumes Arthur (ML.4); see Remark 5.4.6.

items.name: Corollary 5.4.2 (= Theorem 1.0.4): Galois representations for regular L-algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n
items.statement: Let F be totally real or CM and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) with π_∞ regular L-algebraic and π_v unramified at all finite v ∉ S. Then there is a unique continuous semisimple σ_π : G_{F,S} → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) such that for all finite v ∉ S the Satake parameters of π_v agree with the eigenvalues of σ_π(Frob_v).
items.note: The theorem of Harris–Lan–Taylor–Thorne, which Scholze reproves via Theorem 5.4.1; AG2.4 plans the HLTT route (its text says it 'does not use Scholze's torsion Hecke interpolation'), so the statement is planned but not this proof.

items.name: Corollary 5.4.3 (the precise form of Theorem 1.0.3): mod p Galois representations for Hecke eigensystems in torsion cohomology
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. Let ψ : 𝕋_{F,S} → 𝔽̄_p be a system of Hecke eigenvalues with H^i(X_K, ℳ_{ξ,K} ⊗_{ℤ̄_p} 𝔽̄_p)[ψ] ≠ 0. Then there is a unique continuous semisimple σ_ψ : G_{F,S} → GL_n(𝔽̄_p) with det(1 − X Frob_v | σ_ψ) = 1 − ψ(q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v})X + ψ(q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v})X² − ⋯ + (−1)^nψ(q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v})X^n for all finite v ∉ S.
items.note: As PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/69: the determinant specializes to 𝔽̄_p (IHG.5) and a determinant over an algebraically closed field comes from a unique semisimple representation (IHG.1).

items.name: Corollary 5.4.4 as corrected: Hecke-algebra-valued Galois representations for non-Eisenstein maximal ideals
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. Let ψ be as in Corollary 5.4.3 with σ_ψ irreducible, 𝔪 = ker ψ ⊂ 𝕋_{F,S}, 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i) = im(𝕋_{F,S} → End_{ℤ̄_p}(H^i(X_K, ℳ_{ξ,K}))), and N = N([F:ℚ], n) as in Theorem 5.4.1. Then there is an ideal I ⊂ 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i) with I^N = 0 and a unique continuous representation σ_𝔪 : G_{F,S} → GL_n(𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i)_𝔪/I) such that for all finite v ∉ S, det(1 − X Frob_v | σ_𝔪) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n (printed with σ_ψ on the left; sourceIssues E11).
items.note: IHG.1 reconstructs a representation over a complete local ring from a residually absolutely irreducible determinant; uniformity of N in m is what allows passage to 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i).

items.name: Remark 5.4.5: the Calegari–Geraghty existence statement (Conjecture B, modulo a nilpotent ideal)
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. Corollary 5.4.4 holds, with the same proof, with 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i) replaced by 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i)′ = im(𝕋_{F,S} → ∏_m End_{ℤ̄_p/p^m}(H^i(X_K, ℳ_{ξ,K}/p^m))) or by 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ) = im(𝕋_{F,S} → ∏_{i,m} End_{ℤ̄_p/p^m}(H^i(X_K, ℳ_{ξ,K}/p^m))). This gives the Galois representations of Calegari–Geraghty's Conjecture B up to a nilpotent ideal of bounded nilpotence degree, without their expected local properties.
items.note: IHG.2: Hecke algebras acting on all degrees of a bounded complex. The local properties of Conjecture B are not claimed.

items.name: Remark 5.4.6: the unconditional range
items.statement: Setting of §5.2–5.4: F is totally real or CM with maximal totally real subfield F^+; n ≥ 1; h = 2n+1 and d = [F:ℚ](n²+n)/2 if F is totally real, h = 2n and d = [F^+:ℚ]n² if F is CM; S is a finite set of finite places of F stable under complex conjugation containing the places above p and those ramified over F^+; K = K_SK^S ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_{F,f}) is compact open with K^S = ∏_{v∉S} GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}); X_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗_ℚ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K] (a stacky quotient if K is not sufficiently small); 𝕋_{F,S} = ⊗_{v∉S} ℤ_p[GL_n(F_v)//GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]; G_{F,S} is the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S; P_v(X) = 1 − q_v^{(n+1)/2}T_{1,v}X + q_v^{2(n+1)/2}T_{2,v}X² − ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n+1)/2}T_{n,v}X^n, with T_{i,v} the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the Satake variables X_1, …, X_n and q_v the residue cardinality. The results of §5 rest on Arthur (resp. Mok), conditional on the stabilization of the twisted trace formula. By Shin's results (Goldring's appendix; cf. Morel, Corollary 8.5.3) all results stated in §5.4 are unconditional if (i) F is CM and contains an imaginary-quadratic field, and (ii) S is the pullback of a finite set S_ℚ of finite places of ℚ containing p and the places where F/ℚ ramifies; in particular for F imaginary quadratic they hold as stated. Theorem 4.1.1 and Chapter 4 hold verbatim for Shimura varieties of Hodge type attached to unitary similitude groups, so the argument of Chapter 5 applies to them. By a patching argument (Harris–Taylor, Theorem VII.1.9) Corollary 5.4.2 follows for general totally real or CM F, still assuming S comes from a set S_ℚ containing the places where F/ℚ ramifies.
items.note: The CM/unitary branch of TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure consumes exactly ET/AG2's constructed characteristic-zero package; TC's README records that 'Scholze's published Theorem 1.0.3 already distinguishes the branches'.

items.name: Almost mathematics over 𝒪_K: almost zero modules, the category of 𝒪_K^a-modules, and the functors M_*, M_!
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field with ring of integers 𝒪_K and maximal ideal 𝔪_K. An 𝒪_K-module M is almost zero if it is killed by 𝔪_K. The category of almost 𝒪_K-modules (𝒪_K^a-modules) is the quotient of the category of 𝒪_K-modules by the thick subcategory of almost zero modules, with localization N ↦ N^a. The functors M ↦ M_* = Hom_{𝒪_K^a}(𝒪_K^a, M) and M ↦ M_! = 𝔪_K ⊗_{𝒪_K} M_* from 𝒪_K^a-modules to 𝒪_K-modules are right and left adjoint to N ↦ N^a; consequently N ↦ N^a commutes with all limits and colimits. An almost isomorphism is a map whose kernel and cokernel are almost zero.
items.note: P0 nodes almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base (the Serre quotient V^a-Mod, instantiated for (K°, K°°)), almost-hom-and-adjoints ((−)_* right adjoint, (−)_! = m̃ ⊗ M_* left adjoint, (−)^a preserves limits and colimits) and almost-zero-limits-and-colimits. The paper calls N ↦ N^a 'the forgetful functor'. Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti at the baseline. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): Recalled as a definition in the paper and used throughout the range: Lemmas 2.2.5, 2.2.8, 2.2.9(ii), Proposition 2.3.2, Corollary 2.3.5, Lemma 2.3.6, Definition 2.3.8 (good triples), Lemmas 2.3.10–2.3.11, 3.2.27–3.2.32, and Theorem 4.2.1; items /11, /14, /16, /18–/25, /51–/54 are stated in terms of almost isomorphisms.

items.name: The Siegel moduli space X_{g,K^p} over ℤ_(p), its minimal compactification X*_{g,K^p} with ample ω, and the level-K_p spaces
items.statement: Fix g ≥ 1 and a prime p. Let (V, ψ) be the split symplectic space of dimension 2g over ℚ, ψ((a, b), (a′, b′)) = Σ_{i=1}^g (a_i b′_i − a′_i b_i), with self-dual lattice Λ = ℤ^{2g}; let GSp_{2g}/ℤ be the group of symplectic similitudes of Λ, and K^p ⊂ GSp_{2g}(𝔸_f^p) a compact open subgroup contained in {γ ∈ GSp_{2g}(ℤ̂^p) : γ ≡ 1 mod N} for some N ≥ 3 prime to p. X = X_{g,K^p} over ℤ_(p) is the moduli space of principally polarized g-dimensional abelian varieties with level-K^p structure (the Shimura variety of GSp_{2g} acting on the Siegel upper half space). X* = X*_{g,K^p} over ℤ_(p) is its minimal (Baily–Borel–Satake) compactification (Faltings–Chai), carrying a natural ample line bundle ω, given on X_{g,K^p} by the determinant of the sheaf of invariant differentials of the universal abelian scheme; if g ≥ 2 then X*_{g,K^p} = Proj ⊕_{k≥0} H^0(X_{g,K^p}, ω^{⊗k}). All geometric fibres of X* over Spec ℤ_p are normal, with boundary of codimension g. For a compact open K_p ⊂ GSp_{2g}(ℚ_p), X_{K_p} = X_{g,K_pK^p} over ℚ is the moduli space of principally polarized g-dimensional abelian varieties with level-K^p and level-K_p structure, with minimal compactification X*_{K_p} = X*_{g,K_pK^p}.
items.locator: §3.1, pp. 970–971; §3.1, p. 975 (normal geometric fibres and codimension-g boundary)
items.note: PELModuli M5: 'Construct Siegel moduli for every dimension'; ShimuraCompactifications C5: integral PEL toroidal compactifications and 'the Hodge-line positivity and graded-section finite-generation statements that yield the integral minimal compactification, then its projectivity' at good primes (principal polarization, level prime to p). The fact the paper relies on instead of toroidal geometry, normality of all geometric fibres of X* with boundary of codimension g, is not named in C5's text and should be added to its blueprint from this source. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): Every §3 item (/37–/54, /65–/67) states its result on these spaces through a repeated 'Setting of §3' paragraph, but no item records the construction, its status or its owner; the Proj description (used in Lemma 3.2.17 via ampleness of ω) and the normality/codimension-g facts (used in Proposition 3.2.9's application, Lemma 3.2.24 and Lemma 3.2.27) are key inputs.

items.name: L-algebraic automorphic representations of GL_n(𝔸_F)
items.statement: Let F be a number field with adèles 𝔸_F = ∏′_v F_v = 𝔸_{F,f} × (F ⊗_ℚ ℝ), F ⊗_ℚ ℝ ≅ ℝ^{n_1} × ℂ^{n_2}. An automorphic representation π of GL_n(𝔸_F) is L-algebraic if for all infinite places v of F the (normalized) infinitesimal character of π_v is integral.
items.note: AF.4 plans 'infinitesimal characters and cohomological representations; distinguish C-algebraic and L-algebraic normalizations'. Item /1's note already points there; this makes it an item. 'Regular' L-algebraic (Theorem 1.0.4 = Corollary 5.4.2) is made precise in §5. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): Defined in the paper and used in Conjecture 1.0.1 (item /1) and, as regular L-algebraic, in Theorem 1.0.4 = Corollary 5.4.2 (item /110).

items.name: The fake Hasse invariants: the formal model 𝔛*_{K_pK^p} with ω^int and 𝔍, and the Hecke-invariant sections s̄_j
items.statement: Setting of §4.3: (G, D) of Hodge type with a fixed embedding into (Sp_{2g}, D_{Sp_{2g}}), K^p in the level-N subgroup of G′(𝔸_f^p), N ≥ 3 prime to p, n ≥ 1 fixed. Let N′ = C(2g, g), let s_1, …, s_{N′} be the standard sections of 𝒪(1) on ℙ^{N′−1} (ω_Fl = 𝒪(1)|_Fl via Plücker), let U_i ⊂ ℙ^{N′−1} be the affinoid where |s_j| ≤ |s_i| for all j, and let V_i = π_HT^{-1}(U_i) ⊂ 𝒳**_{K^p}, which is affinoid perfectoid by Theorem 4.1.1(i); write s_j also for π_HT^*s_j ∈ H^0(𝒳**_{K^p}, ω_{K^p}). For K_p ⊂ G(ℚ_p) small enough, each V_i is the preimage of an affinoid V_{iK_p} ⊂ 𝒳**_{K_pK^p}, and since colim_{K_p} H^0(V_{iK_p}, ω) → H^0(V_i, ω) has dense image there are sections s_j^{(i)} ∈ H^0(V_{iK_p}, ω_{K_pK^p}) satisfying the conditions of Lemma 2.1.1 with |(s_j − s_j^{(i)})/s_i^{(i)}| ≤ |p^n| on V_i. Pulling back to the preimages Ṽ_{iK_p} ⊂ 𝒳*_{K_pK^p}, Lemma 2.1.1 gives a formal model 𝔛*_{K_pK^p} of 𝒳*_{K_pK^p} with an ample line bundle ω^int_{K_pK^p}, and Lemma 2.1.2 gives an ideal sheaf 𝔍 ⊂ 𝒪_{𝔛*_{K_pK^p}} from the boundary ideal ℐ. These objects do not depend on the choice of the s_j^{(i)}, and G(𝔸_f^p) acts on the tower (𝔛*_{K_pK^p}) with ω^int. The sections s̄_j ∈ H^0(𝔛*_{K_pK^p}, ω^int_{K_pK^p}/p^n) are independent of all choices and commute with the G(𝔸_f^p)-action; they are the substitutes for the Hasse invariant. For k sufficiently divisible, H^1(𝔛*_{K_pK^p}, (ω^int)^{⊗k} ⊗ 𝔍/p^n) = 0.
items.locator: §4.3, proof of Theorem 4.3.1, pp. 1029–1031 (announced in §1, p. 951)
items.note: TC.1 plans the construction: 'compare finite-level sections with infinite-level sections modulo varpi^m. Develop the approximation/extension lemmas that produce finite-level classical sections after twisting by sufficiently high powers of an ample automorphic line bundle. Carry the actual boundary ideal, power of the ample bundle and congruence exponent throughout.' The introduction (p. 951) presents this construction as the reason π_HT matters. Notation 𝒳** as in the extraction; the paper writes an underlined star, as explained in the change to item 68's name. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): This is the paper's substitute for the Hasse invariant and the heart of Theorem 4.3.1, on which Theorem 1.0.5 and all of §5 rest. Item 76 only mentions it in its note, and no item states the construction or its independence and Hecke-invariance properties.

items.name: The Hecke action on p-adic cusp forms H^0(𝒳*_{K_pK^p}, ω^{⊗k} ⊗ ℐ) via trace maps
items.statement: (G, D) of Hodge type as in §4.3. For sufficiently small K_1 ⊂ K_2 ⊂ G(𝔸_f), the map π_{K_1/K_2} : 𝒳*_{K_1} → 𝒳*_{K_2} is locally of the form Spa(B, B^+) → Spa(A, A^+), with A normal, A^+ ⊂ A° open and integrally closed, B a finite normal generically étale A-algebra and B^+ the integral closure of A^+. By Lemma 4.3.2 there are trace maps tr : π_*𝒪_{𝒳*_{K_1}} → 𝒪_{𝒳*_{K_2}}, π_*ℐ_{𝒳*_{K_1}} → ℐ_{𝒳*_{K_2}}, π_*𝒪^+ → 𝒪^+ and π_*ℐ^+ → ℐ^+, where ℐ is the ideal sheaf of the boundary and ℐ^+ = ℐ ∩ 𝒪^+. Since ω_{K_1} = π^*ω_{K_2}, they give tr : π_*(ω_{K_1}^{⊗k} ⊗ ℐ_{𝒳*_{K_1}}) = ω_{K_2}^{⊗k} ⊗ π_*ℐ_{𝒳*_{K_1}} → ω_{K_2}^{⊗k} ⊗ ℐ_{𝒳*_{K_2}}. Taking global sections and composing with pullbacks along Hecke translations defines the action of 𝕋 = ℤ_p[G(𝔸_f^p)//K^p] on H^0(𝒳*_{K_pK^p}, ω^{⊗k}_{K_pK^p} ⊗ ℐ).
items.locator: §4.3, the paragraphs before and after Lemma 4.3.2, pp. 1025–1026
items.note: B5: 'Construct pullback, coefficient identification, and trace along Hecke correspondences … Treat non-neat levels through equivariance/descent'. R3: traces of finite maps and their compatibility with algebraic trace. Lemma 4.3.2 itself is item 77. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): Items 76 (𝕋_cl), 81, 86 (𝕋_{K,k}) and 88–89 use this 𝕋-action on classical cusp forms, but no item defines it. The paper recalls the definition before Lemma 4.3.2.

items.name: The torsion (primitive) comparison theorem with compact supports on the minimal compactification
items.statement: Let K_pK^p ⊂ G(𝔸_f) be sufficiently small, 𝒳*_{K_pK^p} the adic space over C of the (proper, singular) minimal compactification, 𝒵 its boundary and j : 𝒳*_{K_pK^p} ∖ 𝒵 ↪ 𝒳*_{K_pK^p} the open embedding. Then H^i_ét(𝒳*_{K_pK^p}, j_!ℤ/p^nℤ) ⊗_{ℤ/p^nℤ} 𝒪_C^a/p^n ≅ H^i_ét(𝒳*_{K_pK^p}, j_!𝒪^{+a}_{𝒳*∖𝒵}/p^n), naturally in the level. Combined with H^i_c(X_{K_pK^p}, ℤ/p^nℤ) = H^i_ét(𝒳*_{K_pK^p}, j_!ℤ/p^nℤ) (comparison of complex/algebraic/adic, singular/étale cohomology), this is the first step of Theorem 4.2.1.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Theorem 4.2.1, p. 1021 (citing Scholze, Perfectoid spaces: a survey, Theorem 3.13); introduced in §1, p. 949, as the 'first key ingredient' (citing [53])
items.note: No stage owns it. The PadicHodgeTheory--P7 packet records that the primitive comparison theorem (Sch13 Theorem 5.1, relative Corollary 5.11) is needed and that 'no atlas stage currently owns Scholze §5'. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.3 consumes 'the precise primitive comparison' without a supplier. TC.2 builds the comparison diagram of Theorem 4.2.1 from its inputs and 'does not reconstruct' foundational theorems (TC README). Scholze's [53] (p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties) and [54] (the survey) are not in the extraction's prerequisites. Lemma 3.3.4 (item 59) also uses the relative version ([53, Th. 1.3]) for the universal abelian variety. For that degree-one case, T0/T2 plan a Cartier-duality construction instead, so item 59 can stay planned. The natural route is a source or Part II route to the roadmap that should own Scholze 2013 §5. I have not chosen one because routes are not in my assignment. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): The introduction (p. 949) calls it the first key ingredient of Theorem 1.0.5. Without it Theorem 4.2.1, and hence Corollary 4.2.2, Theorem 4.3.1 and all of §5, has no input identifying finite-level compactly supported cohomology with 𝒪^+/p^n-cohomology.

items.name: Hochschild–Serre from compactly supported completed cohomology to finite level, Hecke-equivariantly
items.statement: Situation of the proof of Corollary 5.2.6: G = Res_{F^+/ℚ}G_0 as in §5.1 and K = K_{S^+}K^{S^+} sufficiently small. Assume all places of F^+ above a rational prime ℓ ≠ p, ℓ ≥ 3, lie in S^+. This is achieved by enlarging S^+ without changing K, and the result follows by varying ℓ. Fix a normal compact open subgroup K_pK^p_{S^+} ⊂ K_{S^+} with K^p_{S^+} contained in the level-ℓ subgroup of G_0(𝔸_f), so that K^p_{S^+} ⊂ K_{S^+} is a closed normal subgroup. Then there is a Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence H^i_cont(K_{S^+}/K^p_{S^+}, H̃^j_{c,K^p_{S^+}K^{S^+}}(ℤ/p^mℤ)) ⇒ H^{i+j}_c(X_K, ℤ/p^mℤ), equivariant for the action of 𝕋_{K^{S^+}}. For equivariance, reduce to finite covers with group K_{S^+}/K′_pK^p_{S^+} and use compatibility of trace maps with base change, then pass to the colimit.
items.locator: §5.2, proof of Corollary 5.2.6 and footnote 26, pp. 1044–1045
items.note: CC.6: 'Construct the continuous Hochschild–Serre/descent spectral sequence and its edge maps comparing tower cohomology and fixed-level cohomology … prove functoriality for Hecke maps'. The CC.6 decomposition node hochschild-serre-descent-to-finite-level records the Calegari–Emerton form. ALS.6: 'finite-level descent and the finite-cover Hochschild–Serre application'. The same proof also uses Poincaré duality to pass from T(H^i) to T(H^i_c), which is planned by ALS.5:finite-level-duality ('Hecke adjoint formulas'). The finite-group Hochschild–Serre reduction in the proof of Theorem 5.4.1 (K′ ⊂ K normal with ℳ_{ξ,K′}/p^m trivial) is ALS.6's finite-cover case. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): This is the bridge by which Theorem 4.3.1 (continuity on completed cohomology) and Corollary 4.2.2 (at most d+1 nonzero degrees) control the finite-level Hecke algebra. It is the step giving I^{d+1} = 0 in Corollary 5.2.6, and it appears only in item 97's note.

items.name: Boundary induction for GL_n: determinants on the Borel–Serre boundary cohomology
items.statement: Let F, n, p, S, K = K_SK^S (sufficiently small) be as in §5.4 and 𝕋_{F,S}(K, i, m, ∂) = im(𝕋_{F,S} → End_{ℤ/p^m}(im(H^i(X_K, ℤ/p^mℤ) → H^i(X_K^BS ∖ X_K, ℤ/p^mℤ)))). Then H^i(X_K^BS ∖ X_K, ℤ/p^mℤ) can be expressed, compatibly with the 𝕋_{F,S}-action, in terms of the locally symmetric spaces of GL_{n′}/F with n′ < n. Hence, by induction on n, there are a nilpotent ideal of im(𝕋_{F,S} → End_{ℤ/p^m}(H^i(X_K^BS ∖ X_K, ℤ/p^mℤ))), with nilpotence degree bounded in terms of [F:ℚ] and n, and an n-dimensional continuous determinant of G_{F,S} modulo it with D(1 − X Frob_v) = P_v(X) for all v ∉ S. In particular this holds for 𝕋_{F,S}(K, i, m, ∂) modulo an ideal I_∂.
items.locator: §5.4, proof of Theorem 5.4.1, p. 1058 ('It is an easy exercise …; cf. [18, §3]', i.e. Caraiani–Le Hung, On the image of complex conjugation in certain Galois representations, §3)
items.note: TC.3 is titled 'Boundary induction and determinant factor extraction', but its text treats only the symplectic/unitary parabolics of §5.2. ALS.4 plans the ingredients: the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence of each unipotent/Levi stratum and its Hecke action through parabolic induction and Satake transforms, with modulus and Tate shifts. The paper gives no proof, and the report says the TC.3 design must write it out. I record it as an item rather than a source issue because the author flags it and gives a reference; I did not read that reference. If the lead reads TC.3's text strictly, this item is missing and needs the same route as the TC.3 material. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): This is the second half of the proof of Theorem 5.4.1: the Hecke algebra of H^i(X_K) is glued from the interior part (Theorem 5.3.1) and this boundary part by Chenevier's Corollary 1.14. The main theorem is incomplete without it, and no item states it.

items.name: Chenevier, Corollary 1.14 (descent of a determinant to the subring of its characteristic-polynomial coefficients), with the gluing of determinants modulo I_1 and I_2
items.statement: (As used by Scholze.) Let A → B be an injective map of commutative rings, G a group and D : B[G] → B a d-dimensional determinant with D(1 − Xg) ∈ A[X] for all g ∈ G. Then D comes from a unique d-dimensional determinant A[G] → A. Consequence used in the proofs of Corollaries 5.1.10–5.1.11 and 5.4.2, with Chenevier's Example 2.32: if I_1, I_2 ⊂ T are ideals such that there are determinants with values in T/I_1 and T/I_2 with the prescribed Hecke characteristic polynomials, then there is one with values in T/(I_1 ∩ I_2). The same continuity statements hold for G profinite.
items.locator: Used in §5.1, proofs of Corollaries 5.1.10–5.1.11, pp. 1037–1038; §5.3, proofs of Lemmas 5.3.6–5.3.7, pp. 1051–1052; §5.4, proofs of Theorem 5.4.1, p. 1059, and Corollary 5.4.2, p. 1060 (Chenevier, Corollary 1.14 and Example 2.32)
items.note: The IHG packet node IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.0/determinant-coefficient-subring states Corollary 1.14: 'D factors through a unique C-valued determinant on G' for C the subring generated by the coefficients. IHG.4 plans 'compatible determinants over finite coefficient quotients … passage to inverse limits'. I took the statement from Scholze's use of it and did not read Chenevier. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): This is the gluing tool in Corollaries 5.1.10–5.1.11, Lemmas 5.3.6–5.3.7, Theorem 5.4.1 and Corollary 5.4.2. The extraction cites it only in notes.

items.name: Chenevier, Theorem 2.12: determinants over an algebraically closed field come from unique semisimple representations
items.statement: (As used by Scholze.) Let k be an algebraically closed field, G a group and D : k[G] → k a d-dimensional determinant. Then there is a semisimple representation ρ : G → GL_d(k), unique up to isomorphism, with det ∘ ρ = D. If G is profinite, k carries its topology and D is continuous, then ρ is continuous. For ℚ̄_p-coefficients in Corollary 5.4.2 Scholze deduces continuity, e.g., from Taylor, Galois representations associated to Siegel modular forms of low weight, Theorem 1.
items.locator: Used in §5.3, proof of Lemma 5.3.3, p. 1048 (over the reduced ring Ā, a finite product of copies of 𝔽̄_p); §5.4, proofs of Corollaries 5.4.2–5.4.3, pp. 1059–1060 (Chenevier, Theorem 2.12)
items.note: IHG.1: 'Prove reconstruction over algebraically closed fields up to semisimplification'. The IHG packet's coverage lists 'reconstruction over algebraically closed fields (Theorems 2.12, 2.16)' as remaining in IHG.1. I did not read Chenevier's statement. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): This turns the determinants of Theorem 5.4.1 into the representations of Corollaries 5.4.2–5.4.3, and hence Theorem 1.0.3. It also drives Lemma 5.3.3. Item 111's note mentions it, but no item states it.

items.name: Chenevier, Theorem 2.22(i): residually absolutely irreducible determinants over henselian local rings come from representations
items.statement: (As used by Scholze.) Let A be a henselian local ring with residue field k, G a group and D : A[G] → A a d-dimensional determinant whose reduction to k̄ is the determinant of an absolutely irreducible representation. Then there is a representation ρ : G → GL_d(A), unique up to conjugation, with det ∘ ρ = D; it is continuous when D is. Scholze applies it with A = 𝕋_{F,S}(K, ξ, i)_𝔪/I, a finite local ring, and σ_ψ irreducible.
items.locator: Used in §5.4, proof of Corollary 5.4.4 (printed after Remark 5.4.5), p. 1061 (Chenevier, Theorem 2.22(i))
items.note: IHG.1: 'reconstruction … over complete local rings when residual absolute irreducibility supplies an actual representation'. The packet lists Theorem 2.22 as remaining. Scholze assumes σ_ψ irreducible over 𝔽̄_p, which is absolute irreducibility. I did not read Chenevier's statement. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): This is the only input beyond Theorem 5.4.1 in Corollary 5.4.4 and Remark 5.4.5 (Calegari–Geraghty's Conjecture B up to nilpotents). No item states it.

items.name: Cohomological dimension of the infinite-level minimal compactification is at most d
items.statement: (i) If S = lim_j S_j is a cofiltered inverse limit of spectral spaces along spectral transition maps and every S_j has cohomological dimension ≤ d (H^i(S_j, F) = 0 for all i > d and all abelian sheaves F), then S has cohomological dimension ≤ d. The proof writes F as a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves, each pulled back from some S_j, and computes H^*(S, −) as a colimit. (ii) For K_p small the spectral space |𝒳**_{K_pK^p}| has cohomological dimension ≤ d = dim_ℂ X_K (de Jong–van der Put, Prop. 2.5.8, or Grothendieck's bound for noetherian spectral spaces applied to the formal models); hence so has |𝒳**_{K^p}| = lim_{K_p} |𝒳**_{K_pK^p}|.
items.note: TC.2: 'Establish the cohomological-dimension/amplitude estimates and derived limit bounds used to control the kernel of the Hecke map'. The CC.7 decomposition node records the argument but disclaims it as a CC.7 output. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): This is the whole content of Corollary 4.2.2 (Theorem 1.0.7) beyond Theorem 4.2.1, and through the (d+1)-term filtration it bounds every nilpotence exponent in §5 (2(d+1), 4(d+1), N). Item 74 has it only in its note.

items.name: Clozel: regular L-algebraic cuspidal representations of GL_n contribute to the cohomology of X_K
items.statement: (As used by Scholze, from Clozel, Motifs et formes automorphes, Théorème 3.13 and Lemme 3.14.) Let F be totally real or CM and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) with π_∞ regular L-algebraic, unramified outside S. Then π′ = π|·|^{(n+1)/2} is regular C-algebraic, i.e. cohomological: there is an algebraic representation ξ of Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n with coefficients in ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p, extendable to Res_{𝒪_F/ℤ}GL_n over ℤ̄_p, such that π′ occurs in H^i(X̃_K, ℳ_{ξ,K}) ⊗_{ℤ̄_p} ℂ for some sufficiently small K = K_SK^S and some i. Here X̃_K = GL_n(F)∖[(GL_n(F ⊗ ℝ)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞°) × GL_n(𝔸_{F,f})/K], which is X_K if F is CM and a (ℤ/2ℤ)^{[F:ℚ]}-cover if F is totally real. After twisting by a character 𝔸_F^× → ℤ/2ℤ with prescribed archimedean components, π′ occurs in H^i(X_K, ℳ_{ξ,K}) ⊗ ℂ.
items.note: Uncertain status. AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.4 defines cohomological representations and the C-/L-algebraic normalizations. AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.5 compares relative Lie algebra cohomology of automorphic forms with ordinary cohomology, Hecke-equivariantly. AG2.0 imports 'cohomological infinitesimal characters' from AF.1/AF.4. I found no stage that proves Clozel's theorem that a regular algebraic cuspidal representation of GL_n is cohomological and occurs in cohomology (the search for 'Clozel', 'cuspidal cohomology' and 'regular algebraic … cohomolog' found only AF.4's definitional sentence). AF.4 is the natural owner. The lead should confirm before routing. Added by the review (REV-PAPER-SCHOLZE-15): This is the input that lets Theorem 5.4.1 produce Corollary 5.4.2 (= Theorem 1.0.4) for a given π. Item 110 is planned via the HLTT route (AG2.4), which needs the same fact.

routes.reason: R07.6 plans 'the deformation-theoretic tangent and obstruction calculations' for finite flat and p-divisible groups and already depends on DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0–DD.1 for cotangent complexes. Illusie's obstruction class o ∈ Ext^1(H, K ⊗^𝕃 J) for lifting a morphism u : H → G of flat, finitely presented commutative group schemes along a square-zero thickening, with its functoriality in the thickening (Theorem 3.2.1), is exactly such a calculation, one level more general than p-divisible groups. It belongs inside that layer, not in a new roadmap; the only consumer here is the canonical-subgroup lifting lemma routed to T3, and Remark 3.2.3 shows T3 could instead use DD.0's deformation theory of rings with worse constants.

T3 plans canonical subgroups with quantitative bounds on Hasse neighbourhoods, and PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S1 ('The Siegel construction') consumes T3–T4 for the Siegel tower; but T3's text is written for the Hilbert application of BHW and takes its Hasse neighbourhoods from AdicSpacesPartII R2, HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H2 and ShimuraCompactifications C6, none of which constructs the Hasse invariant of a g-dimensional abelian scheme. Scholze §3.2.1 is the source for the Siegel case: the Hasse invariant Ha(A/S) from Verschiebung, Lemma 3.2.5 (invertible exactly on the ordinary locus) and its extension to the minimal compactification, the lifting lemma Corollary 3.2.2 (with Remark 3.2.3's elementary alternative), and Lemma 3.3.2 on Ha at boundary points, which are missing; and Lemma 3.2.4, Corollary 3.2.6, Definition 3.2.7 and Proposition 3.2.8, which T3 plans, with the explicit constants ε < 1/2 and p^{1−ε}. Theorem 3.2.15 (Frobenius lifts and the anticanonical open immersions, T3/T4), Proposition 3.3.1 (Hodge–Tate filtration through the Raynaud extension, T0) and Lemma 3.3.4 (the period map on points, T2) are planned items for which the paper is the natural source. AF.1 builds the (𝔤, K)-module foundations and AF.4 the infinitesimal characters of cohomological representations; the accepted routes of PAPER-PILLONI-20 (13), PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 (10) and PAPER-BOXER-PILLONI-26 (14) put (limits of) discrete series, their Harish-Chandra parameters and holomorphic limits of discrete series there. Proposition 5.1.1, the unique discrete series π_k of Sp_{2n}(ℝ) or U(n,n) with minimal K-type χ^k and its infinitesimal character, is the next case of the same material.
